record.original_question: Let an abstract argumentation framework be a pair F=(A,R) whose arguments are A and whose attacks are R. For stable semantics, a stable extension is a conflict-free set whose range covers A. A pair of arguments has an implicit conflict when the two arguments never occur together in any stable extension; an argumentation framework is conflict-explicit when every such non-co-occurring pair is connected by at least one attack direction. Is every argumentation framework F=(A,R) stable-equivalent, over the same argument set A, to some argumentation framework F'=(A,R') that is conflict-explicit and has exactly the same stable extensions as F?

evidence.quote: The open problem now consists of proving or disproving whether every AF F has a conflict-explicit AF F 0 over the same arguments with the same stable extensions.
Conjecture 1 For each AF F = (A, R) there exists an AF F 0 = (A, R0 ) which is conflict-explicit under the stable semantics such that st(F ) = st(F 0 ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract argumentation framework is a pair F = (A, R) consisting of a finite set A of arguments and a binary attack relation R ⊆ A × A. Given F, a set S ⊆ A is conflict-free if there are no a, b ∈ S with (a, b) ∈ R. The range of S in F is the set S ∪ {b ∈ A : there exists a ∈ S with (a, b) ∈ R}. A stable extension of F is a conflict-free set S whose range equals A. Write st(F) for the collection of all stable extensions of F.

An (unordered) pair {a, b} of distinct arguments is said to be in implicit conflict (under stable semantics) if there is no S ∈ st(F) with {a, b} ⊆ S. The framework F is conflict-explicit (under stable semantics) if for every such pair {a, b} in implicit conflict, at least one of (a, b) ∈ R or (b, a) ∈ R holds.

Question: Is it the case that for every abstract argumentation framework F = (A, R) there exists an abstract argumentation framework F' = (A, R') on the same set of arguments such that F' is conflict-explicit under the stable semantics and st(F') = st(F)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was refuted: subsequent work on rejected arguments and implicit conflicts showed that under stable (as well as preferred, semi-stable, and stage) semantics, the class of conflict-explicit frameworks does not capture the full expressive power of the semantics, so not every argumentation framework is stable-equivalent to a conflict-explicit one on the same argument set.

status_evidence.title: On rejected arguments and implicit conflicts: The hidden power of argumentation semantics
status_evidence.snippet: Under stable, preferred, semi-stable, and stage semantics neither of the classes [free of rejected arguments / free of implicit conflicts] is able to capture the full expressive power of these semantics.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that every AF is stable-equivalent to a conflict-explicit AF on the same arguments was disproved under stable semantics.
